title: A Liberation Psychology Framework for Supporting Student Activism in Repressive Times
abstract: U.S. universities are increasingly becoming arenas where student activism for self-determination, justice, and liberation confronts escalating institutional and state repression. Pro-Palestinian student protests during the 2023 to 2025 academic years exemplify how university administrations and state actors can intensify measures to suppress dissent. This repression can exacerbate the inherent psychosocial risks of student activism, contributing to adverse mental health outcomes. However, activism can also foster student well-being by cultivating a sense of purpose and solidarity. This manuscript addresses a critical gap in psychological scholarship by proposing Liberation Psychology (LP) as an essential framework for psychology faculty to navigate and support their activist students amidst rising authoritarianism and the corporatization of higher education. I discuss key LP principles, including recovering historical memory, cultivating conscientization (problematization, denaturalization, deideologization, and praxis), prioritizing oppressed majorities, and practicing acompañamiento . Building on these principles, I offer six actionable recommendations for psychology faculty to actively support student activism: engage in conscientization, decolonize curricula, nurture dialogical pedagogy, resist neutrality, practice acompañamiento , and establish the Psychology Department as a site of institutional praxis. To facilitate psychology faculty’s own conscientization process, a series of reflection questions are provided.
